conflict_topics: Friday evening religious observance (Agent D's temple attendance)
swap of Saturday morning and Sunday afternoon shifts
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants gave concrete reasons for constraints (Turn 2 D: 'I go to the temple...', Turn 4 B: '...my kid has swimming lessons'), which grounded proposals.
B proposed a clear three-way swap (Turn 13), and that trade was iterated and confirmed by others.
There is some needless repetition: B repeats the confirmation (Turns 20 and 23) and A repeats 'Okay, settled. I'll send it in.' multiple times (Turns 29, 37, 41).
Roles, facts, and slots stayed consistent and the conversation remained focused on the practical constraint.
evaluation.final_reason: The team agreed a three-way swap that removes the incompatible Friday assignment: Agent A accepted taking the Friday evening slot, Agent D agreed to take Agent B's Saturday morning slot, and Agent B agreed to take Agent A's Sunday afternoon slot. Evidence: B proposed the swap ('...you take Friday evening, Agent D takes my Saturday morning, and I take your Sunday slot?' — Turn 20/23), A accepted ('Yes, that works for me.' — Turn 24), and D had agreed to take Saturday morning earlier ('I can take the Saturday morning slot.' — Turn 11; reaffirmed Turn 25).
position_change_notes: Agent D: initially objected to Friday (Turn 2) but offered flexibility and explicitly agreed to take Saturday morning ('I can take the Saturday morning slot.' — Turn 11; 'Yes, Saturday morning is good for me.' — Turn 25).
Agent B: initially could not do Friday and needed Saturday morning moved (Turn 4), then proposed and agreed to take A's Sunday slot as part of the three-way swap (Turn 13, Turn 20/23).
Agent A: initiated the query and ultimately accepted taking the Friday evening slot ('Yes, that works for me.' — Turn 24).
Agent C: did not change position and explicitly said they could not take another regular slot (Turn 5).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 A: 'Is there a problem with Friday?' — Turn 2 D: 'Yes. I go to the temple with my family on Friday evenings.' (D objects to the assigned Friday slot.)

Turn 3 A: 'Okay. Can anyone swap with Agent D for the Friday slot?' — Turn 4 B: 'I can't do Friday evenings. And I need to move my Saturday morning slot.' (B cannot cover Friday and adds another constraint, making a swap harder.)

Turn 5 C: 'I can't take on another regular slot.' — Turn 6 D: 'I can take another slot. Any other evening is fine, or a weekend.' (D offers flexibility which begins to reduce the conflict; C cannot help.)

Turn 7 A: 'Agent B, what slot can you do instead of Saturday morning?' — Turn 8 B: 'Agent D can take my Saturday morning slot. I can do another weekend slot, or any evening except Friday.' (B proposes a concrete reassignment involving D, lowering the level of conflict.)

Turn 9 A: 'But if Agent D takes Saturday morning, that leaves Friday evening open, and you can't do Fridays.' — Turn 11 D: 'I can take the Saturday morning slot.' (D explicitly agrees to take Saturday morning but Friday remains unresolved.)

Turn 12 A: '...that still leaves the Friday evening slot open.' — Turn 13 B: 'How about this: Agent D takes my Saturday morning, you take Friday evening, and I'll take your slot?' (B proposes a three-way swap, reducing conflict though A hasn't yet accepted.)
Turn 14 A: 'What's my slot on the draft?' — Turn 15 B: 'I don't remember. Does anyone have the roster there?' (Procedural clarification; the proposed swap remains unconfirmed.)

Turn 19 A: 'I'm on Sunday afternoon. You want to take that?' — Turn 20 B: 'Yes, Sunday afternoon is fine. So to confirm: you take Friday evening, Agent D takes my Saturday morning, and I take your Sunday slot?' (A concrete confirmation is proposed; parties have not all verbally accepted yet in this round.)

Turn 23 B: (repeats confirmation) 'Yes... to confirm: you take Friday evening, Agent D takes my Saturday morning, and I take your Sunday slot?' — Turn 24 A: 'Yes, that works for me. Agent D, are you good with Saturday morning?' (A accepts the swap; D had earlier said 'I can take the Saturday morning slot.' (Turn 11). With these acceptances the conflicting assignment is mutually reallocated.)
Turn 25 D: 'Yes, Saturday morning is good for me.' — Turn 26 B: 'Great, so that's settled then.' (Reaffirmation after the agreement; no substantive conflict present.)
Turn 29 A: 'Okay, settled. I'll send it in.' (Administrative closure; no dispute.)
Turn 37 A: 'Okay, settled. I'll send it in.' — Turn 41 A: 'Okay, settled. I'll send it in.' (Repeated confirmations; no substantive conflict.)

substantive_insights: Religious observance (D's Friday temple attendance) created a hard availability constraint that required rearranging three people's weekly slots.
Family obligations (B's child's swimming lessons) limited possible covers and made a straightforward one-for-one swap impossible.
Because one colleague (C) could not take another regular slot, resolving the conflict required a three-way compromise rather than a two-person swap.
